country_overview: India operates under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) 1999 administered by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). Current account transactions are largely liberalised while capital account transactions remain regulated. The framework was updated in 2026 with the Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2026 (effective 1 October 2026).

summary.traveler: Any person may bring foreign exchange into India without limit. However, if foreign currency notes exceed USD 5,000 or the aggregate foreign exchange exceeds USD 10,000 (or equivalent), a Currency Declaration Form (CDF) must be submitted to customs authorities on arrival.
summary.business: All cross-border trade and capital transactions must be routed through Authorised Dealer banks under FEMA. The 2026 regulations introduce targeted updates for exports, imports, service payments, and related business operations.

rules.bring_foreign_currency_in: Foreign exchange may be brought into India without limit. Declaration on the Currency Declaration Form (CDF) is mandatory if foreign currency notes exceed USD 5,000 or the aggregate value of foreign exchange (notes + travellers’ cheques) exceeds USD 10,000.
rules.take_foreign_currency_out: Unspent foreign exchange declared on arrival via CDF may be taken out. Residents must comply with FEMA limits and retain the CDF for reconversion or re-export justification.
rules.cash_declaration_threshold: USD 5,000 (foreign currency notes) or USD 10,000 (aggregate foreign exchange) at entry and exit.
rules.resident_holding_rules: Indian residents face strict controls under FEMA on holding and using foreign currency. General public access to foreign currency accounts is not unrestricted and requires specific approvals or falls under permitted limits.
rules.non_resident_rules: Non-residents (including NRIs/PIOs) may maintain NRE, FCNR (B), or NRO accounts with repatriation rights as per RBI guidelines. Such accounts may be opened and operated through authorised dealers.
rules.business_invoicing_settlement: Domestic transactions must be invoiced and settled in INR. Import and export transactions and cross-border services must be settled through Authorised Dealer banks in compliance with FEMA regulations.
rules.exchange_controls: India maintains a regulated exchange framework under FEMA 1999. Current account transactions are largely liberalised; capital account transactions are subject to regulation and reporting.
rules.banking_conversion_practicality: Foreign exchange transactions are executed through Authorised Dealer banks, licensed money changers, and authorised airports. The Currency Declaration Form (CDF) must be retained for reconversion and compliance purposes.
